newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Tocopilla to build natgas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Tocopilla to build natgas pipeline.

text.p: Recently privatized Chilean electricity firm Tocopilla said it will build a natural gas pipeline across the Andes from northern Argentina to fuel Chile's fast-growing mining industry.

"The board of Electroandina (the new name for Central Termoelectrica Tocopilla SA) has decided to develop a project to build and operate a gas pipeline which will link the province of Salta in Argentina and the port of Tocopilla in our country," said the statement.
The project, to be named Norgas, is the second natural gas pipeline planned for northern Chile.
It raises the specter of a gas pipeline battle similar to that in central Chile last year, when two projects competed to supply Santiago with natural gas.
Power generator Chilgener SA is also planning to build a transmission line to bring power to the mines directly from Argentina.
Tocopilla said it will build two gas-fired plants of 230 megawatts each in Tocopilla, which lies north of Antofagasta.
"Being able to count on these sales contracts guarantees Norgas the finance necessary for the project," it said.
The company did not say when it planned to build the pipeline.

Codelco sold a 51 percent stake in the firm last year for $178 million to a group including Spanish firm Iberola Energia de Espana IBE.MCu, Belgian companies Powerfin SA POWE.BRu and Tractebel TREB.BRu and Chilean company Enagas SA.
Codelco owns 34 percent but plans to sell its shareholding on the bourse this year. The rest is held by workers.
